title: AIMO Trust Extension (v1)
description: The JSON Schema for the `params` object of an A2A AgentExtension whose `uri` is "https://aimo-brain.dev/extensions/trust/v1" (ADR-019 section 6). This document is a DECLARATION of which AIMO BRAIN trust-layer capabilities an agent/organization claims to support and WHERE to independently verify each one -- it is structurally incapable of being, or being mistaken for, the verification result itself. Every boolean-sounding claim in this schema is a claim of SUPPORT, never a claim of CURRENT STATUS: this document never contains fields named 'verified', 'active', or 'authorized', specifically so no implementation can be tempted to read a status flag off the card instead of calling the authoritative source.

schema_version.description: This descriptor's OWN schema version -- independent of trade_protocol's artifact schema version (docs/PROTOCOLS.md) and independent of the JWS artifact-signature spec version (docs/specs/jws-artifact-signatures.md). A verifier must check this before parsing anything else; an unrecognized version is a parse failure, not a best-effort partial read.

organization_id.description: The organization this descriptor is published on behalf of. This is a claim made BY the card's own publisher -- a verifier never trusts this value alone; it is only meaningful once cross-checked against the authoritative registry-api/network-api lookups named in verification_sources.

agent_id.description: Optional: the specific agent this descriptor describes, if narrower than the whole organization.

supported_capabilities.description: Which trust-layer capabilities this agent/organization claims to SUPPORT (per ADR-019 section 3's four-layer model) -- never a claim that any of them currently hold true. Each entry only says 'ask the authoritative source named in verification_sources about this layer'; it is never itself the answer.

verification_sources.description: The ONLY place this descriptor is allowed to point a verifier -- never an inline status. Maps each of the four trust-layer concepts to the live HTTP endpoint that authoritatively answers it. A verifier MUST call these endpoints and MUST NOT short-circuit on anything else present in this document.

discovery.description: Authoritative source: the agent's own A2A Agent Card URL, fetched directly. Proves only that the endpoint exists and speaks A2A -- nothing about trust (ADR-019 section 5).

identity.description: Authoritative source: registry-api's agent-status endpoint. Proves endpoint control and private-key control (ADR-015/016) -- NOT the organization's legal identity (ADR-019 section 5).

delegation.description: Authoritative source: network-api's delegations.json / introspection endpoints. Proves a specific key may sign a specific scope of artifact types on this organization's behalf (ADR-017/018) -- not permission to transact.

trading_relationship.description: Authoritative source: network-api's party/operator-only relationship-status endpoint (ADR-019 section 6/8). Proves counterparty ELIGIBILITY only -- a specific commitment additionally requires in-scope delegation, a live identity/delegation check, an OPA decision, required approval, and the commitment protocol's own semantics (ADR-019 section 5). This endpoint is itself access-controlled: only a party to the relationship, or an AIMO operator, may query it -- this descriptor cannot be used to bypass that, since it only names the endpoint, which still enforces its own access control independently.

freshness_policy.description: States, for each verification source, that it is subject to the SAME freshness/fail-closed rules as everywhere else in this system (ADR-017/018/019) -- a bounded-TTL cache for most lookups, and a mandatory fresh (uncached) check for commitment-adjacent artifact types. This descriptor never overrides or relaxes those rules; it only restates that they apply.

cache_ttl_seconds.description: The bounded staleness window a verifier MAY tolerate for a cached read of any verification_sources endpoint, for non-commitment-adjacent artifact types only.

commitment_adjacent_artifact_types.description: Artifact types (per trade_protocol) for which a verifier MUST force a fresh, uncached check of identity/delegation status, per ADR-017/018's existing rule -- restated here, not redefined.

endpoint.description: The live HTTP endpoint a verifier calls to independently check this claim. Never a value that itself states the result.
